To: Cedarbrook Pharmacy page
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Corvane children's ibuprofen recall — which lots, and what to do today

Important update for parents — please read and share.

WHAT THE RECALL COVERS
Corvane is voluntarily recalling the oral dosing syringe that came in the box with Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (berry), 120 mL bottle, in two lots only: CV6114A and CV6114B (expiry 08/2027).

THE MEDICINE IS FINE. IT'S THE SYRINGE.
The printing on the syringe barrel is wrong: the marks are labelled at half their true volume. The line marked 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL, and the line marked 5 mL actually measures 10 mL. A caregiver following the syringe exactly as printed would give about twice the intended dose. The liquid itself meets all specifications — it is not contaminated, and it is not expired. Please do not throw the bottle away.

WHAT TO DO NOW
1. Check the lot number on the bottom of the box (it's also on the bottle label). Only CV6114A and CV6114B are affected. If your lot is anything else, you're fine.
2. If it's an affected lot: stop using the syringe that came in the box, throw it away, and use a correctly marked oral syringe. We have FREE replacement 10 mL syringes at the pharmacy — no receipt and no purchase needed. The first batch arrives before noon today; more are coming, and you can pick up at the counter any time we're open.
3. Bring the box and bottle back for a full refund on the recalled product. We're open extra on Saturday 10 am–4 pm for exchanges and refunds, and we can take returns during regular hours too.
4. If your child has already had a dose from an affected syringe, please call the Ontario Poison Centre (1-800-268-9017, 24 hours) or your child's doctor BEFORE the next dose, and let them assess your child. Each case depends on your child's weight, how many doses were given, and other health factors, so nobody can judge that safely from a social media post. Don't give another dose until the poison centre or your doctor says it's okay.
5. Call 911 or go to the ER if your child is very sleepy or hard to wake, is vomiting blood, is not passing urine, or has a seizure.

ABOUT NOT BEING CALLED
We were notified by the manufacturer on the evening of Friday, November 6, and removed the affected stock and put up signs at the store on Saturday, November 7. Most over-the-counter sales don't include a phone number, so we were not able to call individual households. We know that wasn't good enough, so we're posting here as well. If you call the pharmacy and ask for the pharmacist on duty, or come in with the box, we'll go through it with you face to face.
